name: SSI2100
description: First new bucket brigade delay design in decades, built on a modern CMOS process rather than a legacy vintage clone. A 512-stage switched-capacitor delay chain runs from a single TTL/CMOS clock (1kHz-2MHz), with an on-chip clock driver and tetrode bias generator removing the need for a companion BBD clock IC or an external legacy VGG (14/15 V+) supply. A patent-pending scheme allows multiple SSI2100s to be daisy-chained for longer delays without recalibrating inputs/outputs, and exposes intermediate feedback taps for reverb/psychoacoustic effects. Single 5V operation and an 8-lead SOP package make it far more compact than classic BBDs like the MN3007/MN3005 it functionally succeeds.

pins.name: GND
pins.description: analog signal ground; connect with a short, low-inductance trace or closely-spaced vias to a ground plane

pins.name: GCAP
pins.description: gain capacitor enable; tie to GND for standard (0dB-ish) gain or to V+ for high gain (~6dB). Must not be left floating

pins.name: SIGNAL IN
pins.description: audio signal input to the internal sample-and-hold; requires a 3.20V DC bias and a low-impedance drive source. Max signal range 440mVpp

pins.name: VTBIAS
pins.description: internally-generated tetrode bias voltage (~14/15 of V+, biases internal tetrode transistors); connect a 3.3uF capacitor to GND (add a parallel 100nF ceramic for very high clock frequencies)

pins.name: SIG OUT 2
pins.description: delay chain output when CLK IN is high; source-follower, anti-phase with SIG OUT 1, needs an external load

pins.name: SIG OUT 1
pins.description: delay chain output when CLK IN is low; source-follower, anti-phase with SIG OUT 2, needs an external load

pins.name: V+
pins.description: +5V supply only; recommend a local 100nF X7R ceramic decoupling capacitor plus 10uF+ bulk decoupling, short low-inductance trace to ground

pins.name: CLK IN
pins.description: clock input to the internal clock generator, which produces two anti-phase buffered clocks for the delay chain; TTL/CMOS compatible at both 3.3V and 5V logic levels

SOP-8.notes: Per Sound Semiconductor's own Pin Connections diagram and Pin Descriptions table (Rev 2.2, October 2025), 8-lead SOP, top view. SSI package ID 'PSL8', compliant with JEDEC MS-012-AA.

extra.clock frequency range: 1kHz to 2000kHz (2MHz); will run outside this range with some degradation
extra.clock logic levels: VIH 2.5V min, VIL 1.5V max (TTL/CMOS, 3.3V and 5V compatible)
extra.signal input DC bias: 3.20V required at pin 3, needs a low-impedance bias source
extra.input/output -3dB bandwidth: 15kHz min (at fCLK=40kHz test condition; scales with clock frequency, filter to half fCLK to satisfy Nyquist)

typical_application: Analog delay line for chorus, flanging, reverb, and slapback/echo effects in synths and effects pedals; direct modern replacement for legacy 512-stage BBDs (e.g. MN3007) with a simpler support-circuit footprint since the clock driver and VGG-equivalent tetrode bias are on-chip. Needs an anti-aliasing filter ahead of SIGNAL IN and a reconstruction filter after the outputs, both set near the clock's Nyquist frequency (see datasheet Figure 1 application circuit).
gotchas: single 5V rail only, not split supply; absolute max on any pin is 7V
SIGNAL IN (pin 3) needs a precise 3.20V DC bias from a low-impedance source, not just AC coupling; get this wrong and the sample-and-hold mis-biases
GCAP (pin 2) must be tied to GND or V+, never left floating, or gain/behavior is undefined
as a sampled-data device it needs Nyquist-correct anti-alias and reconstruction filtering around half the clock frequency; skipping either lets clock-rate energy or aliased signal through

the two SIG OUT pins are anti-phase source followers that need an external load and often benefit from the optional trim pot (Figure 2) to null residual clock breakthrough from output-transistor mismatch
VTBIAS (pin 4) requires an external 3.3uF cap to GND; add a parallel 100nF ceramic if running near the top of the clock range
a genuinely new CMOS design, not a clone of a legacy BBD, though it targets the same use cases as parts like the MN3007/MN3005 with far less external clock/bias support circuitry
sold only directly by Sound Semiconductor and its authorized resellers
